subject: Maths
title: Dividing decimals
subtitle: Decimals — All Operations · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can divide decimal numbers by whole numbers and by other decimals.

key_vocab.definition: To divide a decimal by a whole number, use short/long division keeping the decimal point in the same position in the answer.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can divide decimal numbers by whole numbers and by other decimals.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: divide a decimal -- To divide a decimal by a whole number, use short/long division keeping the decimal point in the same position in the answer.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
If dividing by a decimal, multiply both numbers by 10 or 100 to make the divisor a whole number.
3.6 ÷ 0.6 = 36 ÷ 6 = 6
Make the divisor whole

Key examples:
  ✓ 8.4 ÷ 4 = 2.1  (decimal point stays)
  ✓ 3.6 ÷ 0.6 = 36 ÷ 6 = 6  (multiply both by 10)
  ✓ 12.5 ÷ 0.5 = 125 ÷ 5 = 25  (equivalent division)
  ✗ 8.4 ÷ 4 = 21  (forgot decimal point)
  ✗ 3.6 ÷ 0.6: only multiply top by 10  (must multiply both)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – decimal by whole number
  Calculate 9.6 ÷ 4
  Set up short division: 9.6 ÷ 4
  9 ÷ 4 = 2 r 1; bring down 16 ÷ 4 = 4
  Keep decimal point aligned: 2.4
  = 2.4
  (The decimal point stays in the same place.)

Example 2 – by a single-digit
  Calculate 15.75 ÷ 5
  15 ÷ 5 = 3
  7 ÷ 5 = 1 r 2; 25 ÷ 5 = 5
  = 3.15
  = 3.15
  (Work digit by digit; carry remainders.)

sections.title: More decimal ÷ whole number
sections.content:
Keep the decimal point in line.

(a) 15.75 ÷ 5
(b) 24.8 ÷ 4
(c) 3.42 ÷ 6
(d) 27.36 ÷ 8

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ 8.4 ÷ 4 = 2.1
✗ 3.6 ÷ 0.6 = 0.6
✓ Multiply both by 10 to remove decimal divisor
✗ When dividing by 0.5, the answer is smaller
✓ 4.8 ÷ 0.6 = 48 ÷ 6 = 8
